knowledge_point.title: Finding the Rank or Nullity of a Matrix Given a Description of the Column or Null Space

question.:question/worked-solution:
According to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

For the given matrix, we have $n=4,$ since this is the number of components in each of the vectors of the null space. 

Also, since 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 3 \\ -3 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}\,|\,\,{x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R\}
$$

we conclude that $\text{nullity}(A)=3.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A) & =n \\ \text{rank}(A)+3 & =4 \\ \text{rank}(A) & =4-3 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: real vector spaces; full column rank parameter coefficient matrix
